01 · YOUR EXACT SLIDE

First, learn the route through the slide.

This slide contains a lot of information. Your audience should never have to decide where to look. You will give them a route.

THE AUDIENCE ROUTE

Do not follow the boxes randomly.

Recommended spoken order: Problem → objective → impact → scope → planning → team / close.

This order creates a story: why the project exists → what success looks like → why it matters → boundaries → plan → people.

“Let me first explain the problem we are trying to solve. Then I’ll show you the target, the business impact, the project scope and the main milestones.”

02 · RETRIEVAL BEFORE NEW LANGUAGE

Start with familiar ideas before adding more precision.

Answer orally first. No timer. Then reveal the model.

Répondez d'abord à l'oral. Pas de chronomètre. Puis affichez le modèle.

1

State the problem

How would you explain that the current processing time is too long?

Model

“Currently, the average processing time is 5.3 days, which is too long to support on-time delivery.”

2

State the target

How would you compare the current KPI with the target?

Model

“The current average is 5.3 days, and our target is 2 days.”

3

Move to the next block

How would you move from the problem to the objective?

Model

“With that problem in mind, let me show you the operational objective.”

04 · OPEN THE MEETING BEFORE THE SLIDE

Give the room a clear map.

Your opening has four jobs: welcome → purpose → route → permission to interact.

Votre introduction a quatre fonctions : accueil → objectif → parcours → invitation à interagir.

WELCOME“Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here.”

Warm, short and easy.

PURPOSE“I’d like to walk you through our Kaizen #3 project on NNC shop processing time.”

Tell the room why you are speaking.

ROUTE“I’ll start with the problem, then the target, the scope and the project plan.”

Make the order predictable.

INVITE“Please feel free to jump in if you’d like me to clarify anything.”

Make interaction welcome.

Build your opening one decision at a time

1 · Welcome
2 · Purpose
3 · Route
4 · Invite
Supported model · B1

“Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining. I’d like to give you a clear overview of our NNC processing-time improvement project. I’ll start with the current problem, then the target, the business impact, the scope and the main milestones. Please feel free to ask questions as we go.”

Natural model · B1+/B2

“Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here. I’ll keep this focused and walk you through the main logic of the project: why it is needed, what success looks like, where the scope starts and stops, and how the improvement work is planned. Please jump in if you’d like me to clarify anything.”

05 · PROBLEM DESCRIPTION

Explain the problem before explaining the solution.

The slide gives two key facts: the average overall processing time is 5.3 days, and it states 31 days for reworked parts. Your spoken version should make the consequence clear without adding a cause that is not on the slide.

Le slide donne deux faits clés : 5,3 jours de temps moyen global et 31 jours pour les pièces retouchées. Expliquez la conséquence sans inventer une cause qui n'apparaît pas sur le slide.

1

CURRENT STATE

“Currently, the average overall processing time for a NNC is 5.3 days.”

→
2

CONSEQUENCE

“This is too long to ensure on-time delivery of the parts.”

→
3

EXAMPLE / SCALE

“The slide also shows 31 days for reworked parts.”

USEFUL GRAMMAR

too + adjective + to + verb

“The processing time is too long to ensure on-time delivery.”

Use this structure when a current condition prevents the desired result.

Do not overclaim:
“The slide tells us the processing time is too long. It does not, by itself, explain every root cause behind that delay.”

Check the message before speaking

1. What is the current average processing time shown?

2. Which sentence is the safest description of the consequence?

3. What can you safely say about 31 days?

07 · SCOPE

Make the project boundary easy to understand.

Keep internal terms exactly as written if there is no approved English expansion. Your job is to explain what is included and excluded — not to redefine the acronyms.

IN SCOPE

The slide includes

Nozzle and Blade CFM56 & LEAP; parts oriented to PNR; Y6 for non-conformity laboratory.

OUT OF SCOPE

The slide excludes

Parts with CSC case (2%); Y7 sample labo.

NATURAL SCOPE VERBS

covers · includes · excludes

“The project covers…”

“The scope includes…”

“It excludes…”

“The project scope covers the items listed here. It includes nozzle and blade CFM56 and LEAP, together with the other cases shown on the slide. It excludes parts with a CSC case and Y7 sample labo.”

Scope precision

1. Which statement is supported?

2. What is explicitly out of scope?

3. You are not sure what an internal acronym officially expands to in English. What is safest?

08 · DMAIC PLANNING

Present the milestones without reading a calendar.

The slide lists Kick-off, Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve and Control. Use the date as support, but focus on the sequence.

26/06/2026

Kick-off

Project start

30/07/2026

Define

Define phase milestone

30/08/2026

Measure

Measure phase milestone

30/09/2026

Analyze

Analyze phase milestone

16/10/2026

Improve

Improve phase milestone

+30 / 60 / 90 days

Control

Follow-up cadence shown on slide

TENSE CHOICE

Completed or planned? Use what is actually true.

If completed: “We completed the Measure phase on August 30.”

If planned: “The Analyze milestone is planned for September 30.”

If you only want to report the slide: “The slide lists the Analyze milestone for September 30.”

Important: the check marks on the slide are presentation markers. Do not automatically say every phase is completed unless that is factually true in the meeting.

Milestone language

10 · GRAMMAR THAT SUPPORTS THIS SLIDE

Choose the form from the meaning.

The presentation moves between current facts, project history, planned milestones and possible outcomes.

CURRENT FACTPresent simple

“The current average is 5.3 days.”

COMPLETED MILESTONEPast simple

“We completed the Measure phase on…”

PROGRESS TO NOWPresent perfect

“We have identified…” — only if true.

PLANNED / POSSIBLEFuture / conditional

“The next milestone is planned for…” / “If we reduce…, it could…”

HIGH-VALUE STRUCTURES

for this exact presentation

too + adj + to: too long to ensure…

from … to …: from 5.3 days to 2 days

by …: reduce by 3.3 days

includes / excludes: scope boundaries

Careful language:
“Based on the slide…”
“At this stage…”
“The slide shows…”
“I don’t want to speculate…”

Guided grammar · immediate feedback

1. The current average SPT for NNC ___ 5.3 days.

2. The target is to reduce the average from 5.3 days ___ 2 days.

3. That means reducing the current average ___ 3.3 days.

4. The current processing time is ___ on-time delivery.

5. The project scope ___ nozzle and blade CFM56 and LEAP.

6. The scope ___ parts with a CSC case.

7. If Analyze is still a planned milestone, say: “The Analyze milestone ___ September 30.”

8. If the processing time falls, on-time delivery ___.

11 · KEEP THE AUDIENCE WITH YOU

Transitions turn six boxes into one story.

Use one sentence to close the current block and point to the next one.

PROBLEM → OBJECTIVE

“With that problem in mind, let me show you the operational objective.”

OBJECTIVE → IMPACT

“So why does closing that gap matter? There are both operational and financial reasons.”

IMPACT → SCOPE

“To keep the project focused, the slide also defines a clear scope.”

SCOPE → PLANNING

“Once the boundary is clear, the next question is how the work is structured over time.”

PLANNING → TEAM

“Finally, let me show you how the project is sponsored and managed.”

TEAM → CLOSE

“That gives you the overall project picture. Let me quickly recap the key point before we open the discussion.”

Choose the best meeting move

1. A useful but off-topic question interrupts the Problem block.

2. You finish the problem statement and want to move to the KPI target.

3. You have reached the Team block and want to close.

12 · UNEXPECTED QUESTIONS

A question does not require an instant perfect answer.

Use a repeatable structure: acknowledge → clarify / think → answer → evidence → next step or check.

1

Acknowledge

“That’s a good question.”

→
2

Clarify / think

“When you say target, do you mean the 2-day KPI?”

→
3

Answer

Give one clear point first.

→
4

Evidence

Use only what you know or what the slide shows.

→
5

Check / next

“Does that answer your question?”

NO ROOT CAUSE ON SLIDE

Why is processing time 5.3 days?

“The slide establishes the current level, but it doesn’t show the detailed root-cause breakdown. I don’t want to speculate. That analysis belongs to the improvement work.”

TARGET RATIONALE NOT SHOWN

Why exactly 2 days?

“The slide defines 2 days as the project target. The rationale behind that number isn’t shown here, so I’d rather verify the agreed basis than invent an explanation.”

31-DAY FIGURE

Is 31 days the average for every part?

“No. The slide associates the 31-day figure with reworked parts. The overall average shown is 5.3 days.”

SCOPE

Why are CSC cases excluded?

“The slide shows that parts with a CSC case are out of scope, but it doesn’t give the reason for that boundary. I can confirm the rationale separately if needed.”

Choose the most credible response strategy

1. “Why is the current processing time 5.3 days?”

2. “Why was 2 days selected?”

3. “So every NNC takes 31 days?”

4. You get a detailed technical question that is not answered on the slide and you are not certain.

ONLY AFTER THE COACHING ABOVE

Press “New question” when you are ready.

Keep the response roadmap visible. This is practice, not a test.

Supported complete model · B1

Opening
“Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining. I’d like to give you a clear overview of our NNC processing-time improvement project. I’ll start with the problem, then the target, the business impact, the scope and the main milestones. Please feel free to ask questions as we go.”

Problem
“Currently, the average overall processing time for a NNC is 5.3 days. This is too long to ensure on-time delivery of the parts. The slide also highlights 31 days for reworked parts, which shows why this project is important.”

Objective + impact
“The main KPI is average SPT for NNC. The current level is 5.3 days, and the target is 2 days. So we have a 3.3-day gap to close. Operationally, the slide links the project to part serviceability, respect of commitments and customer satisfaction. Financially, it also highlights a reduction in parts holding costs.”

Scope
“To keep the project focused, the slide defines a clear scope. It includes nozzle and blade CFM56 and LEAP, together with the other cases listed here. It excludes parts with a CSC case and Y7 sample labo.”

Planning
“The planning follows the DMAIC sequence shown at the bottom of the slide. Kick-off is dated June 26, followed by Define on July 30, Measure on August 30, Analyze on September 30 and Improve on October 16. Control is shown as follow-up at plus 30, 60 and 90 days.”

Team + close
“Finally, the project sponsor is Alexis Garsaud. I’m managing the project, and the team members are listed here on the slide. So the key point is simple: the current 5.3-day average is well above the 2-day target, and this project gives us a clear framework to close that gap. That’s the overview I wanted to share. I’m happy to take your questions.”

Natural complete model · B1+/B2

“Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here. I’ll keep this focused and walk you through the main logic of the project: why it is needed, what success looks like, where the scope starts and stops, and how the work is planned.

Let me start with the problem. The average overall processing time for a NNC is currently 5.3 days, which the slide identifies as too long to ensure on-time delivery. For reworked parts, the slide shows a much longer figure of 31 days. That gives us the starting point for the project.

In KPI terms, the objective is very clear: move from a current average of 5.3 days to a target of 2 days. In other words, there is a 3.3-day gap to close. The reason this matters is broader than the KPI itself. Operationally, the slide links the project to part serviceability, respect of commitments and customer satisfaction. Financially, it also points to reducing parts holding costs.

To keep the work focused, the slide defines the scope explicitly. It includes the nozzle and blade CFM56 and LEAP items and the other cases listed here, while parts with a CSC case and Y7 sample labo are outside the scope.

The project then follows the DMAIC sequence. The slide lists Kick-off on June 26, Define on July 30, Measure on August 30, Analyze on September 30 and Improve on October 16, followed by Control at plus 30, 60 and 90 days. I would describe a milestone as completed or planned according to its actual status at the time of the meeting.

Finally, the project sponsor is Alexis Garsaud. I’m managing the project, and the team members are listed here. So the key takeaway is that we have a clearly defined problem, a measurable 2-day target, a bounded scope and a structured improvement plan. That’s the overall picture. I’m happy to take your questions.”
